correctness.rationale: For every epsilon>0, kappa>=0, delta!=0, direct differentiation verifies v=delta exp((y^2-1)/(2 epsilon)) and u/v=kappa (y^3-y)/(3 epsilon). Squared Euclidean norm equals exp((y^2-1)/epsilon)[1+kappa^2 y^2(y^2-1)^2/(9 epsilon^2)]. It is less than 1 at y=0, equal to 1 at y=1, strictly greater than 1 at y>1. On 0<y<1, t=(1-y^2)/epsilon converts norm return to the level condition kappa=3 sqrt((exp(t)-1)/((1-epsilon t)t^2)). This function diverges at both interval endpoints. Its logarithm has positive second derivative -1/(4sinh^2(t/2))+epsilon^2/(1-epsilon t)^2+2/t^2>0, proving unique minimum and exhaustive 0,1,2 interior root counts. The nondegenerate second derivative yields square-root fold. At epsilon=0, minimizer t0 in (1,2) solves (2-t0)exp(t0)=2, and implicit-function/envelope differentiation yields kappa_epsilon=kappa0(1+t0 epsilon/2+O(epsilon^2)). The standalone verifier passed 336 exact rational identities and 95 representative numeric checks; it is corroborative only. No analytic inference from finite enumeration or failed solver was used.

value.rationale: The shear y^2-1/3 is, up to scaling, the least-degree nonconstant even polynomial whose integral over the symmetric [-1,1] passage vanishes. This deliberately probes a natural cancellation boundary: the spectral balance and net shear both return to zero at y=1, yet sufficiently strong variable Jordan amplification creates two additional norm recrossings on the repelling side. The exact all-epsilon 1/2/3 trichotomy, unique fold, square-root splitting and first-order singular shear threshold quantify an otherwise hidden nonnormal obstruction to a single entry-exit description. The fact is not merely a computation at an arbitrary isolated parameter: it classifies a continuous, naturally normalized family and supplies an analytic benchmark for variable nilpotent passage.
